editorial:
Imagine the stress of breaking up with your partner right before your sister's big wedding weekend. That is exactly where Lori and Doug find themselves. Instead of dealing with the drama and awkward questions from their families, they decide to play a dangerous game. They agree to fake their relationship for a few days so they do not ruin the party. You will find yourself laughing at the tension as they try to act lovey-dovey while actually being totally over each other. The vibe is light and breezy, making it the perfect choice for a lazy Friday night when you just want something easy to watch.

What really makes this work is the chemistry between the two leads; they make the fighting and the flirting feel totally real. The pacing is quick, though some of the jokes are a bit predictable. If you enjoy rom-coms where the couple spends the whole time arguing before realizing they still have a spark, you will love this. It is a great pick for a date night or a solo binge.
endingExplained: After spending the whole weekend lying to everyone, Lori and Doug realize that their fight was just a misunderstanding. They rediscover why they fell in love in the first place while pretending to be happy. In the final scenes, they stop the act and decide to actually get back together for real. They apologize for their mistakes and end the movie as a happy couple, proving that their bond was stronger than their breakup.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cute romantic comedies with a bit of family chaos.
